newsitem.title: GERMANY: German public TV station tops private channel.
newsitem.headline: German public TV station tops private channel.

text.p: German public television broadcaster ARD said on Friday it had succeeded in unseating previous number one station RTL in the July ratings race.
With a 15 percent viewer share during the month, ARD edged past RTL, which posted a 14.8 percent share. ARD cited figures provided by the GfK market research institute.

"The numbers show that public stations have a chance even with the stiffest competition and that apparently the public considers our programming indispensible," ARD general manager Udo Reiter said in a statement.
ARD was citing figures provided by the GfK market research institute.
ProSieben, the top station in the ProSieben Media AG stable, said it had begun to close the gap in July between it and RTL among the key target group of viewers, those under 50 years old.
Among viewers under 50, ProSieben said it had posted a 14.6 percent share, down from 15.2 percent in June, also using data provided by the GfK.
RTL won a 16.5 percent share of the target group, down from 17.9 percent from its June stand, ProSieben said, adding that all the major German private stations had posted losses for the month.

Private channel SAT1 drew 11.6 percent of viewers under 50, the most important group for advertisers, ProSieben said. Kabel 1, the second of the ProSieben group's stations, achieved a 4 percent share of the target group.
